title: Where a law page BINDS -- a host's scoped law, declared once and served to every runtime at the directory it governs
description: A law page is one grammar: host-owned prose, the same form as the root law page. A SCOPE adds exactly one proposition to it -- the directory below which it binds -- and nothing else, so a module's own laws have one home (the page) and one placement (this row). Every runtime the host serves receives the page at the place that runtime reads nested instructions, as a projection; no runtime file is ever hand-written. The root of the host is not a scope: it is the briefing every served runtime already receives, and a scope naming it is refused rather than ordered against it.

dir.description: Host-relative directory, forward slashes, no trailing '/'. Must exist, lie inside the host, and lie outside every kit plane -- a pinned or taken copy is not the host's to govern.

page.description: Host-relative path of the law page this scope serves -- the same grammar as the root law page.

says.description: Why this directory carries laws of its own, in one sentence.
